indexPrompt.ptft-fine-tuning-memory: A decoder-only model has a 50,000-token vocabulary, width 2560, 32 blocks, feed-forward width 10,240 and 2,048 learned positions. Count its parameters and work out the training memory for full fine-tuning, for training only the top k blocks, and for LoRA of rank 16 on the query and value projections of every block.
indexPrompt.ptft-greedy-against-beam: A toy model always writes exactly three tokens: the first is A with probability 0.6 or B with 0.4, the second is drawn from fixed conditional probabilities given the first, and the third from fixed conditional probabilities given the whole prefix. Compare the sequence greedy decoding writes with the sequence beam search of width 2 returns.
indexPrompt.ptft-lora-or-unfreeze: A decoder has 24 blocks of width 2048 and feed-forward width 8192. Plan P unfreezes the last block and keeps everything else frozen; plan Q freezes the whole model and adds a LoRA update of rank r to all six matrices of every block. Find the largest r for which plan Q trains no more parameters than plan P.
indexPrompt.ptft-loss-floor: A team makes training text for a small language model from a random process over 8 tokens: after the current token, with probability one half the next token is the current token plus one wrapping from 7 to 0, and otherwise it is drawn uniformly from all 8 tokens. Work out the average loss the lesson's table model approaches, and decide which of three reported runs must have a bug.
indexPrompt.ptft-temperature-and-nucleus-order: A model's next-token distribution over six tokens is 0.34, 0.24, 0.20, 0.13, 0.08 and 0.01 from most to least probable. Two pipelines apply a temperature of 0.5 and top-p at 0.9 in opposite orders, renormalizing at each step; work out what each one can sample.
